benchmark_metadata.title: GraphRAG vs Plain Vector RAG Local Benchmark
benchmark_metadata.author: Harsh Maurya
benchmark_metadata.hardware: Local Consumer Hardware — NVIDIA RTX 3060 (6GB VRAM), AMD Ryzen 5, 16GB RAM
benchmark_metadata.corpus: Multi-document corpus (30 academic & technical papers on distributed systems and neuromorphic computing, ~125,000 tokens)

sample_evaluations.question: How does Floquet engineering in graphene lattices modulate the topological phase boundary described by Kitamura?
sample_evaluations.ground_truth: Floquet periodic optical driving induces a non-trivial Chern number by opening dynamical bandgaps at Dirac points, transitioning the lattice into an anomalous Floquet Chern insulator.

plain_rag.response: Floquet engineering drives graphene using laser fields which affects conductivity and Dirac points, but the exact topological phase boundary depends on temperature.
plain_rag.hallucination_note: Falsely attributed topological transition primarily to temperature rather than non-trivial Chern number induction.

graph_rag.response: Through periodic time-dependent optical driving, dynamical bandgaps open at Dirac crossings. This induces an effective Floquet-Magnus Hamiltonian with a non-trivial Chern invariant (C = 1), defining the anomalous topological insulator boundary.
graph_rag.hallucination_note: Clean multi-hop traversal along (Floquet Driving -> Dirac Crossing -> Chern Invariant).

sample_evaluations.question: What is the primary constraint when deploying Louvain community detection on consumer 6GB VRAM GPUs alongside an Ollama LLM?
sample_evaluations.ground_truth: Memory contention between the quantized model weights (~2-4GB) and large adjacency matrix sparse allocations, requiring offloading graph partition calculation to CPU RAM.

plain_rag.response: The main constraint is model latency, which slows down vector cosine similarity search in CUDA cores.
plain_rag.hallucination_note: Confused vector search latency with VRAM memory allocation contention.

graph_rag.response: VRAM allocation limits: the 4-bit quantized model weights consume ~2.1GB, leaving ~3.9GB. Large graph adjacency matrices risk triggering CUDA Out-Of-Memory, necessitating NetworkX Louvain computation on host CPU RAM with selective subgraph tensor offloading.
graph_rag.hallucination_note: Accurately resolved memory budgeting between host RAM and CUDA VRAM.

sample_evaluations.question: Which cryptographic primitive does FormattingBuddy use to secure WASM-extracted OCR text before local persistence?
sample_evaluations.ground_truth: AES-GCM 256-bit encryption with PBKDF2 key derivation via the browser's native Web Crypto API.

plain_rag.response: FormattingBuddy stores text in browser localStorage using base64 encoding.
plain_rag.hallucination_note: Falsely claimed insecure base64 storage; missed AES-GCM Web Crypto implementation.

graph_rag.response: FormattingBuddy employs 256-bit AES-GCM authenticated encryption through the browser's native Web Crypto API, deriving encryption keys via PBKDF2 with client-side salting before writing to IndexedDB.
